text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The government will decide by the year's-end whether Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd would be given a bigger stake in ailing Perwaja Steel under a privatisation-and-rescue plan, said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on a visit to the steel plant.

-- Maju Holdings has projected Perwaja Steel will make a profit of 100 million ringgit in 1998, which will increase to 200 million a year by 2000, said Maju's managing director and Perwaja CEO Abu Talib Mohamed.

-- The Malaysian cabinet has directed the Primary Industries Ministry to hold a meeting with local companies that have overseas timber concessions to work out a strategy to counter negative foreign attacks on their logging practices, said Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik.
